evidence: Receiving DO2 crash at t=48.2h: 11.5 -> 3.97 mg/L, continuing decline to 2.78 mg/L at t=52h, vs 2.0 mg/L minimum
Source batches at comparable age (48-52h) held 10.3-11.3 mg/L DO2, confirming receiving-specific anomaly
Forward model: transfer multiplier estimated 0.471 since t=48h
Model predictions (min DO / below-limit h / product kg): keep 1.22/5.0/172.1; combined 1.23/7.0/173.7; reduce_feed 1.07/9.2/172.6; increase_air 1.07/9.2/172.4; strong_feed_reduction 1.45/4.8/181.6
Sensitivity: strong_feed_reduction is the only action with a feasible ensemble member (min DO up to 2.47 mg/L)
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 crashed at t=48h to ~3 mg/L and is declining toward the 2.0 mg/L minimum, unlike source batches at the same age (9-12 mg/L); a detected transfer-capacity drop (multiplier ~0.47) is the likely cause. Forward-model comparison shows strong_feed_reduction (0.6x feed, 1.15x air) gives the best oxygen margin (min DO 1.45 vs 1.07-1.23 for alternatives), the fewest below-limit hours (4.8), the highest retained product mass (181.6 kg vs ~172-174 kg), and the only fully feasible sensitivity member. It reduces OUR enough to counteract the transfer loss while retaining production; keep or milder actions risk a deeper, longer oxygen violation and product loss.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is a nominal source-calibrated prediction, not the hidden realization; even the best action is predicted to transiently breach 2.0 mg/L (~4.8 h). If the DO crash was a transient sensor/transfer glitch, the strong feed cut sacrifices some productivity unnecessarily. DO trajectory at 52h (2.78 mg/L) leaves little margin for waiting on an assay, so prompt action was preferred over requesting an extra product assay.
